# FDG8039

> DO use the “Collection” suffix in names of types implementing `IEnumerable` (or any of its descendants) and representing a list of items.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.4.1 Naming Custom Collections.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1710
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Test profile: none, because CA1710 also enforces the other suffixes of Table 3-5, and chapter 3 is off in the test profile. CA1710 reports a type that implements ICollection, ICollection&lt;T> or the non-generic IEnumerable and whose name does not end with Collection (or Dictionary, Set, Stack or Queue). In a probe with SDK 10.0.402 it did not report a type that implements only IEnumerable&lt;T>, as OrderCollection does in the body, nor a type derived from List&lt;T> or Collection&lt;T> (CA1710's default dotnet_code_quality.CA1710.exclude_indirect_base_types = true; setting it to false reports such types, but it would change CA1710 for chapters 3 and 7), so coverage is partial. CA1710 cannot tell a list of items from a custom data structure (FDG8040); a report on a data structure is not a violation and can be suppressed. FDG3058 is the same guideline in chapter 3. Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1710 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public class OrderCollection : IEnumerable<Order> { ... }
public class CustomerCollection : ICollection<Customer> { ... }
public class AddressCollection : IList<Address> { ... }
```
